meta.title: AI Foundations Roadmap
meta.subtitle: From zero to a solid base in ML, deep learning, LLMs and applied AI. 16 weeks · ~10 hrs/week · theory-first · 100% free resources.
meta.assumes: Comfortable with multivariable calculus and linear algebra. No prior ML assumed.

changelog.title: Roadmap created
notes: Initial 16-week plan across 6 phases: foundations, classical ML, deep learning, transformers & LLMs, applied AI & agents, and four specialisation weeks (vision, RL, ML systems, safety & interpretability).
All resources are free to access.

phases.title: Orientation & toolkit
phases.summary: Fill the one maths gap most people have (probability), get fluent with NumPy, and get the lay of the land.

weeksList.title: Probability, NumPy & the big picture
weeksList.goal: Be able to reason about random variables, expectations, Gaussians and Bayes' rule, and to write vectorised NumPy.

items.title: Intro to Large Language Models (1-hr talk)
items.note: Motivation: where this whole roadmap is heading.

items.title: Probabilistic Machine Learning: An Introduction — Ch. 1
items.note: Free PDF. A crisp map of supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning.

items.title: Mathematics for Machine Learning — Ch. 6 (Probability & Distributions)
items.note: Free PDF. The probability you need for everything that follows. Skim Ch. 5 (vector calculus) as a refresher.

items.title: CS229 Probability Theory Review
items.note: A compact reference sheet to keep open.

items.title: Python & NumPy Tutorial
items.note: Broadcasting and vectorisation are the key ideas.

items.title: A Visual Introduction to Machine Learning
items.note: Beautiful scrolly explainer of decision trees and overfitting.

items.title: Essence of Linear Algebra
items.note: Geometric intuition for the linear algebra you already know. Watch at 1.5×.

weeksList.build: Set up Python + Jupyter (or Google Colab). Simulate draws from a few distributions, check the law of large numbers, and code Bayes' rule for a medical-test example.

phases.title: Classical machine learning
phases.summary: The core ideas every later topic reuses: loss functions, maximum likelihood, generalisation, regularisation and the bias–variance trade-off. Andrew Ng's CS229 is the backbone.

weeksList.title: Supervised learning I: linear models & the probabilistic view
weeksList.goal: Derive linear and logistic regression from maximum likelihood and train them with gradient descent.

items.title: CS229 (Autumn 2018) — Lectures 1–4
items.note: Intro, linear regression, locally weighted & logistic regression, Newton's method, GLMs.

items.title: CS229 Lecture Notes — Ch. 1–3
items.note: Work through the derivations with pen and paper; this is where the theory sticks.

items.title: An Introduction to Statistical Learning (Python) — Ch. 2
items.note: Free PDF. The gentlest treatment of what 'learning' and 'error' mean.

items.title: ISLP — Ch. 3–4 (Linear regression, Classification)
items.note: A more statistical angle on the same models; good for intuition.

weeksList.build: Implement linear and logistic regression from scratch in NumPy with batch gradient descent, then check your answers against scikit-learn.

weeksList.title: Supervised learning II: generalisation, kernels & trees
weeksList.goal: Understand why models overfit, how to measure it, and the main model families beyond linear models.

items.title: CS229 (Autumn 2018) — Lectures 5–9
items.note: GDA & Naive Bayes (5), SVMs (6), kernels (7), data splits & cross-validation (8), decision trees & ensembles (9).

items.title: CS229 Lecture Notes — generative models, kernels, regularisation
items.note: Read alongside the lectures above.

items.title: ISLP — Ch. 8 (Tree-based methods)
items.note: Decision trees, bagging, random forests and boosting. Still the default for tabular data.

items.title: A Few Useful Things to Know About Machine Learning
items.note: Twelve hard-won lessons. Reread it at the end of the roadmap.

items.title: ISLP — Ch. 5–6 (Resampling, Regularisation)
items.note: Bootstrap, CV, ridge and lasso in depth.

items.title: XGBoost: A Scalable Tree Boosting System
items.note: The gradient-boosting workhorse of industry and Kaggle.

weeksList.build: Pick a tabular dataset (e.g. from the UCI repository). Compare logistic regression, an SVM, a random forest and gradient boosting using k-fold cross-validation in scikit-learn.

weeksList.title: Unsupervised learning & ML practice
weeksList.goal: Cluster, reduce dimensionality, fit latent-variable models with EM, and diagnose a failing model.

items.title: CS229 (Autumn 2018) — Lecture 12: Debugging ML models & error analysis
items.note: Ng's practical playbook for when things don't work. Very high value.

items.title: CS229 (Autumn 2018) — Lectures 13–15: k-means, EM, factor analysis, PCA & ICA
items.note: EM is the first 'latent variable' idea; it comes back in VAEs and diffusion.

items.title: ISLP — Ch. 12 (Unsupervised learning)
items.note: PCA and clustering with clear intuition.

items.title: How to Use t-SNE Effectively
items.note: Interactive. Teaches you not to over-read embedding plots.

items.title: Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning — Ch. 9 (Mixture models & EM)
items.note: Free PDF. The classic rigorous treatment of EM.

items.title: Understanding Machine Learning — Ch. 2–5 (PAC learning, VC dimension)
items.note: Free PDF. Learning theory: worth it if you're heading for a research masters.

weeksList.build: Run PCA on MNIST and plot the first two components; implement k-means from scratch and compare it with scikit-learn's GaussianMixture.

phases.title: Deep learning foundations
phases.summary: Neural networks, backpropagation, optimisation and CNNs. Simon Prince's Understanding Deep Learning is the theory spine; Karpathy's Zero to Hero series makes it concrete.

weeksList.title: Neural networks & backpropagation
weeksList.goal: Understand what an MLP computes, why depth helps, and derive backprop as reverse-mode autodiff.

items.title: Neural Networks, Ch. 1–4
items.note: The best visual intuition for gradient descent and backprop.

items.title: Understanding Deep Learning — Ch. 3–5 & 7
items.note: Free PDF. Shallow nets, deep nets, loss functions, gradients and initialisation. Rigorous but readable.

items.title: Building micrograd: the spelled-out intro to neural nets & backprop
items.note: Builds an autograd engine in ~100 lines. Code along.

items.title: CS231n notes: Backpropagation, intuitions
items.note: Gradient flow through common gates, with worked examples.

items.title: Yes you should understand backprop
items.note: Short: why leaky abstractions bite.

weeksList.build: Finish your own micrograd, then train a 2-layer MLP on a toy 2D dataset and plot the decision boundary.

weeksList.title: Training deep nets: optimisation, regularisation & PyTorch
weeksList.goal: Know how to make deep nets train well (optimisers, initialisation, normalisation, regularisation) and be fluent in basic PyTorch.

items.title: Understanding Deep Learning — Ch. 6, 8, 9
items.note: Fitting models, measuring performance (incl. double descent) and regularisation.

items.title: makemore Part 1 (bigrams) & Part 2 (MLP)
items.note: Learn PyTorch tensors while building a character-level language model. Start with Part 1.

items.title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
items.note: The default optimiser. Focus on Algorithm 1 and the bias correction.

items.title: A Recipe for Training Neural Networks
items.note: Practical wisdom you'll return to for years.

items.title: PyTorch: Learn the Basics
items.note: Tensors, datasets, autograd, the training loop.

items.title: makemore Part 3: Activations, gradients & BatchNorm
items.note: Deep intuition for why initialisation and normalisation matter.

items.title: Why Momentum Really Works
items.note: Interactive. The maths of momentum, nicely visualised.

items.title: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting
Batch Normalization
items.note: Read for the idea; the original 'internal covariate shift' explanation is now disputed.

weeksList.build: Rewrite your Week 5 MLP in PyTorch. Train on MNIST with SGD, then Adam; add dropout and weight decay and compare learning curves.

weeksList.title: Convolutional networks & residual architectures
weeksList.goal: Understand convolutions, inductive bias, and why residual connections unlocked very deep networks.

items.title: CS231n notes: Convolutional Neural Networks
items.note: The standard reference on CNN layers and their shapes.

items.title: Understanding Deep Learning — Ch. 10–11
items.note: Convolutional networks and residual networks.

items.title: ImageNet Classification with Deep CNNs (AlexNet)
items.note: The paper that kicked off the deep learning era.

items.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition (ResNet)
items.note: Residual connections show up in every modern architecture, transformers included.

items.title: CS231n (2017) lectures 5 & 9: CNNs and CNN architectures
Feature Visualization
items.note: What CNN neurons respond to. An early taste of interpretability.

weeksList.build: Train a small CNN on CIFAR-10 in PyTorch. Then fine-tune a pretrained ResNet-18 from torchvision and compare.

phases.title: Transformers & large language models
phases.summary: From word embeddings and attention to GPT, then scaling laws and post-training (RLHF). This is the core of modern AI.

weeksList.title: Sequences, embeddings & attention
weeksList.goal: Understand how text becomes vectors, why RNNs struggled, and how attention solved it.

items.title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space (word2vec)
Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
items.note: Where attention was introduced.

items.title: But what is a GPT? & Attention in transformers, visually explained
items.note: Two videos, watched in order.

items.title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Recurrent Neural Networks
items.note: A historical classic.

weeksList.build: Implement single-head scaled dot-product attention in NumPy and check it against torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention.

weeksList.title: Transformers in depth: build a GPT
weeksList.goal: Know every component of a decoder-only transformer and how pretraining with next-token prediction works.

items.title: Attention Is All You Need
items.note: Probably the most important paper on this roadmap.

items.title: Let's build GPT: from scratch, in code, spelled out
items.note: Code along. By the end you'll have trained a small transformer yourself.

items.title: Transformer Explainer (interactive)
items.note: Runs GPT-2 in your browser so you can watch the tensors flow.

items.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers
items.note: The encoder-only counterpart; still the basis of most embedding models.

items.title: Let's build the GPT Tokenizer
items.note: Many LLM quirks trace back to tokenisation.

items.title: The Annotated Transformer
items.note: The original paper, line by line in PyTorch.

items.title: The Transformer Family, Version 2.0
items.note: A survey of architectural variants. Use it as a reference.

weeksList.build: Finish the GPT build. Train it on a text corpus of your choice and try changing the context length, number of heads and depth.

weeksList.title: LLMs: pretraining, scaling & post-training
weeksList.goal: Understand how frontier LLMs are made: scale, data, compute-optimal training, instruction tuning and RLHF.

items.title: Deep Dive into LLMs like ChatGPT
items.note: The full lifecycle: data, tokenisation, pretraining, SFT, RL. The best single overview there is.

items.title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners (GPT-2)
Language Models are Few-Shot Learners (GPT-3) — §1–3
items.note: In-context learning appears.

items.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
items.note: Read with Chinchilla, which corrects it.

items.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback (InstructGPT)
items.note: The recipe behind ChatGPT.

items.title: Direct Preference Optimization
items.note: RLHF without the RL. Elegant derivation.

items.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
items.note: How almost everyone fine-tunes in practice.

items.title: RLHF: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback

weeksList.build: Use a scaling-law formula to estimate the compute-optimal model size and token count for a few compute budgets. Optionally, LoRA fine-tune a small open model in a free Colab GPU.

phases.title: Applied AI: reasoning, RAG & agents
phases.summary: How modern reasoning models work, and how to build reliable systems on top of LLMs: prompting, evals, retrieval, tools and agents.

weeksList.title: Reasoning models, prompting & evals
weeksList.goal: Understand test-time compute and RL-trained reasoning, and learn to prompt and evaluate LLM systems rigorously.

items.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in LLMs
DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via RL
items.note: An open, detailed account of training a reasoning model with RL.

items.title: Why We Think
items.note: A survey of test-time compute and reasoning.

items.title: Prompt engineering overview & guides
items.note: Practical, model-agnostic techniques.

items.title: Your AI Product Needs Evals
items.note: The most important habit in applied AI.

items.title: Patterns for Building LLM-based Systems & Products
items.note: Evals, RAG, fine-tuning, caching, guardrails, all in one place.

items.title: The Llama 3 Herd of Models
items.note: An unusually complete public account of building a frontier-class model. Skim it.

weeksList.build: Run a small open model locally (e.g. with Ollama) and write a 30-example eval for a task you care about. Compare plain prompting with chain-of-thought.

weeksList.title: Retrieval, tools & agents
weeksList.goal: Build intuition for RAG, tool use, agent loops and context engineering, and for when not to use an agent.

items.title: Introducing Contextual Retrieval
items.note: Practical RAG improvements with measured results.

items.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
items.note: The foundational agent-loop pattern.

items.title: Building Effective Agents
items.note: Workflows vs agents, and why simple usually wins.

items.title: Effective Context Engineering for AI Agents
LLM Powered Autonomous Agents
items.note: Planning, memory and tool use.

items.title: Agents
items.note: Tools, planning and failure modes.

items.title: Model Context Protocol: Introduction
items.note: The emerging standard for connecting models to tools and data.

items.title: Hugging Face AI Agents Course
items.note: Free, hands-on, with a certificate.

items.title: SWE-bench: Can LMs Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
items.note: How agentic coding is measured.

weeksList.build: Build a tiny RAG system over your own notes (a local embedding model plus cosine search), then wrap it as a tool in a minimal agent loop of about 50 lines.

phases.title: Specialisations
phases.summary: One focused week each on computer vision & generative models, reinforcement learning, ML systems / MLOps, and safety & interpretability. The four weeks can be done in any order.

weeksList.title: Computer vision & generative models
weeksList.goal: Understand vision transformers, joint image–text embeddings and diffusion, the basis of modern image and video generation.

items.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision (CLIP)
items.note: Contrastive image–text learning; the root of most multimodal models.

items.title: Understanding Deep Learning — Ch. 18 (Diffusion models)
items.note: The clearest derivation of diffusion available.

items.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
items.note: Stable Diffusion.

items.title: An Introduction to Flow Matching
items.note: The training objective behind many current image and video models.

items.title: Segment Anything
items.note: Foundation models for segmentation.

items.title: U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation
items.note: The backbone of classic diffusion models.

weeksList.build: Use CLIP (via Hugging Face transformers) for zero-shot classification on a few images of your own. Optionally, train a tiny DDPM on MNIST.

weeksList.title: Reinforcement learning
weeksList.goal: Grasp MDPs, value functions, policy gradients and PPO, which is the RL behind RLHF and reasoning models.

items.title: RL Course — Lectures 1–2 (Intro, MDPs)
items.note: The classic RL course. Lectures 3–7 are a great follow-up.

items.title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction — Ch. 3 & 6
items.note: Free PDF. Finite MDPs and temporal-difference learning. Skim Ch. 4 (DP).

items.title: Spinning Up in Deep RL — Introduction to RL (Parts 1–3)
items.note: A concise bridge from theory to deep RL, including policy-gradient derivations.

items.title: Playing Atari with Deep Reinforcement Learning (DQN)
Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms (PPO)
items.note: The RL algorithm in classic RLHF.

items.title: DeepSeekMath (introduces GRPO)
items.note: The critic-free RL variant behind many reasoning models.

items.title: RLHF Book
items.note: Free online. Connects this week back to LLM post-training.

items.title: Hugging Face Deep RL Course
items.note: Hands-on with Gymnasium environments.

weeksList.build: Implement tabular Q-learning on Gymnasium's FrozenLake, then REINFORCE on CartPole.

weeksList.title: ML systems, MLOps & efficient inference
weeksList.goal: Understand what it takes to ship and serve ML: data and feature pipelines, monitoring, GPU performance, parallelism, quantisation and LLM serving.

items.title: Hidden Technical Debt in Machine Learning Systems
items.note: Why the model is the smallest box in the diagram.

items.title: Rules of Machine Learning
items.note: 43 rules from production ML at Google.

items.title: Made With ML — MLOps lessons
items.note: Design → data → training → testing → serving → monitoring.

items.title: Making Deep Learning Go Brrrr From First Principles
items.note: Compute-, memory- and overhead-bound workloads explained.

items.title: How to Scale Your Model — Parts 1–3
items.note: Rooflines, TPUs/GPUs and transformer maths for scaling.

items.title: Efficient Memory Management for LLM Serving with PagedAttention (vLLM)
items.note: KV-cache management, the core problem of LLM serving.

items.title: The Ultra-Scale Playbook: Training LLMs on GPU Clusters
items.note: Data, tensor, pipeline and context parallelism, with measurements.

items.title: FlashAttention
items.note: IO-aware attention. A good example of systems thinking.

items.title: Full Stack Deep Learning (2022)
items.note: Lectures on the whole lifecycle of ML products.

weeksList.build: Take your Week 7 CNN or Week 9 GPT, export it, serve it behind a tiny FastAPI endpoint, and measure latency before and after int8 quantisation.

weeksList.title: AI safety & interpretability
weeksList.goal: Know the main problems in AI safety and the core ideas of mechanistic interpretability: circuits, superposition and sparse features.

items.title: Concrete Problems in AI Safety
items.note: The classic problem framing.

items.title: Zoom In: An Introduction to Circuits
A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits
items.note: The residual stream view of transformers. Your Week 9 work pays off here.

items.title: Scaling Monosemanticity
items.note: Sparse autoencoders find interpretable features in a production model.

items.title: On the Biology of a Large Language Model
items.note: Attribution graphs that trace model internals for real behaviours.

items.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
items.note: RLAIF, which builds on your Weeks 10 and 14.

items.title: Toy Models of Superposition
items.note: Why neurons are polysemantic.

items.title: Alignment Faking in Large Language Models
How to Become a Mechanistic Interpretability Researcher
items.note: A roadmap if this week hooks you.

items.title: ARENA (Alignment Research Engineer Accelerator)
items.note: Free, rigorous exercises in interpretability and RL for alignment.

items.title: International AI Safety Report
items.note: A broad, policy-oriented view of risks and mitigations.

weeksList.build: Use TransformerLens on GPT-2 small to find an induction head: run a repeated random-token sequence and look at the attention patterns.

items.title: Let's reproduce GPT-2 (124M)
items.note: A full, efficient training run end to end.

items.title: CS336: Language Modeling from Scratch
items.note: Build every piece of an LLM stack. Lectures and assignments are public.

items.title: Practical Deep Learning for Coders
items.note: Top-down and code-first; a good balance to this theory-first roadmap.

items.note: Free online.

items.title: How to Read a Paper
items.note: The three-pass method. Two pages.

items.title: Deep Learning: Foundations and Concepts

items.title: Probabilistic Machine Learning: Advanced Topics

items.title: Hugging Face Daily Papers

items.title: Anthropic courses (prompting, tool use, evals)
